d: Sensing Hwon's inner turmoil, Woon delivers Wol's letter to him. Drawn to the handwriting and phrasing that feel hauntingly familiar, Hwon finds himself shaken. Meanwhile, Bogyeong detects the strange tension between Hwon and the shaman, and Queen Dowager Yoon orders that the consummation date be moved forward.

When Nokyoung warns Yangmyung not to form any emotional ties with Wol, he pushes back fiercely. Determined to resolve the growing chaos, Wol announces her intention to leave Seongsucheong. At the same time, Hwon discovers troubling inconsistencies in Yeonwoo's final letter.

Having resolved to leave Seongsucheong, Wol asks Nokyoung for one last chance to see Hwon, unable to push him from her thoughts. Meanwhile, Bogyeong learns from Queen Dowager Han that the date for her consummation with Hwon has been set.

On the night Hwon is to consummate his marriage with Bogyeong, he collapses after being struck by an unknown curse. Seizing the moment, Bogyeong schemes to place the blame on Wol. Seeking the truth behind Yeonwoo's death, Hong Gyu-tae visits a physician, while Wol is falsely accused and dragged to the State Tribunal.

Late at night, Hwon visits Wol in her prison cell and coldly orders her to distance herself from him. Yet as Wol is being transferred to the Bureau of Beneficence, she is abducted. Hearing the news, Yangmyung rushes out in shock—only to be stopped in his tracks by Woon.
A film capturing a journey across Korea, collecting the diverse sounds of everyday life and bringing them together to create a single piece of music.

With all her memories restored, Yeonwoo meets Seol and asks about what truly happened the day she underwent the shamanic initiation rite. Meanwhile, Hwon orders Hong Gyu-tae to investigate in detail what occurred on the night the Crown Princess collapsed from her sudden illness.
